evidence: createApp(): `const app = express(); app.use(express.json());` sets up the framework (infrastructure)
Route registrations such as `app.post('/projects/:projectId/tasks', controllers.tasks.create)` hand requests to controllers without any logic of their own (transport routing)
`app.use((_req, res) => { res.status(404).json({ error: 'Route not found' }); })` is an HTTP-level fallback, a transport concern
The Controllers interface only groups controller dependencies for composition
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts only sets up the HTTP transport layer. It creates the Express app, adds JSON body parsing, maps routes to controller handlers, adds a 404 fallback and registers the error-handling middleware. All of this is framework and transport wiring, which is what the infrastructure layer is for. The file has no business rules, no domain decisions, no orchestration of use cases and no persistence logic. The 404 response is a transport concern, not a business rule.
